title: Monads as a pluggable notion of function application

title: Investor defends JustFab against scam claims

title: Speculative credit card pricing startup idea
why: Speculative startup brainstorm with no evidence or insight a reader would learn from.

title: Why JavaScript debugging tools are unusually strong
why: Browser devtools offer source maps, remote mobile debugging, profiling and time-travel debugging, making JS unusually debuggable.

title: Personal Google Fi porting horror story
why: Personal complaint about one carrier's support; the anecdote carries no general lesson.

title: Why Mt. Gox's txid fix matters for exchanges
why: Transaction malleability changes txids; a normalized hash index lets exchanges and explorers reliably track withdrawals and deposits.

title: Personal story about a rare surname
why: Personal memoir about name and identity with no technical or informational takeaway.

title: Personal account of testing as a bright kid
why: Personal grievance about schooling and testing; mostly anecdote without a broader lesson.

title: Outsider opinion on American society
why: Opinion and generalization about American culture and class; no substantive lesson.

title: How fair use's four factors apply to Google Books
why: Walks through the four statutory fair use factors and explains why transformative, public-benefit copying can outweigh full-text copying.

title: Why Google's hiring equated impact with shipped code
why: Measuring get-things-done by shipped code made non-coders like designers hard to evaluate, exposing a flaw in the process.

title: Unit tests as documentation of behavior, not proof
why: Treat any interface as a unit and tests as statements of 'when I do X, the result is Y' rather than checks of correctness.

title: Author's preference for Perl over alternatives
why: Personal language preference argued from experience; mostly an opinion rather than a transferable lesson.

title: Concerns about SpaceX and local residents
why: News and environmental/political concern about a launch site; no technical lesson.

title: Why canvas-rendered GUIs hurt accessibility and UX
why: Canvas or WebGL widgets bypass the DOM accessibility layer and native input behavior, so platform affordances like cut/paste and scrolling get lost.

title: EU Article 11 text excludes mere hyperlinks
why: Article 11 grants press publishers rights but exempts hyperlinks with individual words and private non-commercial use; news coverage ignored this.

title: Argument about whether to find a cofounder
why: Argumentative back-and-forth over startup advice with no concrete, transferable insight.

title: Why RubyGems fights fleet-wide OS deployment
why: Language package managers bypass system deployment tooling, so unattended installs across many servers need manual steps, unlike apt.

title: Why lock files still matter beyond functional package managers
why: Hashing builds is powerful, but app developers still need lock files and resolution to swap dependency versions without rewriting packages.

title: Expert sources beat popular coverage on science and policy
why: IPCC summary reports and think tanks like Brookings and CSIS are far more informative than popular climate and foreign policy coverage.

title: Most famous inventors came from modest backgrounds
why: Aristocrats were overrepresented but a minority; many scientists were sons of teachers, bakers, carpenters and shopkeepers.

title: Why a CMS should expose an API, not serve pages
why: Keeping content editing separate from rendering makes the CMS safer to leave unexposed and lets editors and front-end teams work independently.

title: Work-hour limits did not change surgical mortality
why: Studies found no mortality difference after resident work-hour restrictions, a counterintuitive result a neurosurgeon explains via attending care.

title: Why HP profits more from ink than printers
why: Refill ink and cartridge margins make HP effectively an ink seller, so blocking cheap refills protects its main revenue stream.

title: Opinion on startup ideas and corporate customers
why: Opinionated advice about salesmen and corporate decision-makers with no concrete, verifiable lesson.

title: Practical lessons on measurement and rollouts
why: Measure rather than guess, and turn systems on before they are ready so real usage data drives fixing the underlying data.

title: How to start learning math: logic and proofs first
why: Branches of math share ground; learn logic, theorems and proofs as a language, then study one branch with a core set of introductory ideas.

title: Why SSA and functional programming were different projects
why: SSA was built to speed compiler dataflow analysis; its link to functional programming was a theoretical overlay, not the original design goal.

title: Opinion against running everything in the browser
why: Opinion piece against web-based software; argues preference rather than teaching a concrete technical idea.

title: Critique of Wolfram's fundamental theory claims
why: Analogy-driven rebuttal and opinion about a theory; argues rather than explains a technical mechanism.

title: Personal account of moving from US to Europe
why: Personal life-decision anecdote and preferences; no transferable technical or informational lesson.

title: Treat hiring as tracked funnel marketing
why: Track hiring like conversion optimization: measure funnel stages, write candidate-focused job posts, and check which screens predict later success.

title: Many mocks signal code that needs restructuring
why: A unit test needing several mocks usually means the function does too much; splitting it makes tests faster, clearer and easier to rewrite.

title: Anecdotes from prime-prize claimants
why: Entertaining anecdotes about persistent prize claimants; no technical lesson for the reader.

title: Feature story about Walter Pitts
why: Biographical feature praising an underdog story; it recounts events rather than teaching a concept.

title: Mandatory doc comments bloat simple code
why: Forcing boilerplate doc comments onto self-explanatory methods adds noise that buries the few comments that actually matter.

title: Gendered expectations of confidence at work
why: Social commentary on gender and workplace perception; not a technical or informational lesson.

title: Personal account of a breakdown and police visit
why: Personal narrative about a mental health episode and police contact; no general lesson.

title: Critique of Orwell's essay on language
why: Stylistic argument and rebuttal of an essay; opinion-driven with no concrete new knowledge.

title: Phone photos fail when printed or viewed large
why: Phone images look fine on small screens but degrade at 8x10 or monitor sizes, a gap a working pro observes from editing weddings.

title: Reflections on PHP and language popularity
why: Personal reflection on language popularity indexes and PHP history; opinion with little transferable insight.

title: Random variables defined by repeated measurement
why: A random variable is a quantity that varies across repeats; its distribution is defined by probabilities for X being at most x, not a set of weighted samples.

title: Argument over the FSF's RYF certification
why: Polemic on free-software certification and tactics; argumentative rather than explanatory.

title: Advice on overcoming loneliness via a partner
why: Personal life advice and opinion about relationships; not a technical or informational lesson.

title: Argument about tone and moral frameworks
why: Heated exchange about tone and morality with no informational content a reader would learn from.

title: Rails and Django differ in template logic constraints
why: Django restricts template logic to enforce separation, while Rails allows arbitrary Ruby; Django apps share one project DB, not true pluggability.

title: Personal anecdote about eating less
why: Single-person diet anecdote with personal rules; the advice is situational and not broadly instructive.

title: Why the HURD's microkernel design struggled
why: Insider account: the microkernel promised user control but faced context-switch costs, while GNU libc work proved lasting.

title: Why newcomers find Erlang hard to approach
why: Praises Erlang's small syntax and built-in concurrency, but notes weak beginner tooling and marketing hurt adoption among outsiders.

title: Identity-aware proxies beat per-app OAuth logins
why: Put apps behind a proxy that authenticates once and signs identity tokens, with trusted devices, so apps skip repeated login prompts.

title: Recursion is different from iteration, not harder
why: Recursion's essence is using a thing in its own definition, which is unfamiliar even though repetition is familiar; that is why students struggle.

title: A tiny tool pulled in dozens of packages
why: glslify, a simple file-loading helper, drags in a large transitive dependency tree, showing the hidden cost of npm dependencies.

title: Controlled studies challenge static typing's benefits
why: Common sense says static typing prevents runtime errors, but controlled experiments show the benefits are less clear than assumed.

title: Personal take on Surface hardware and sales
why: User opinion and rant about product timing and marketing; subjective with no broadly applicable lesson.

title: Commentary on an encrypted-data criminal case
why: Opinion and speculation about a legal case's evidence and defendant; not an informative technical lesson.

title: Defensive political argument about China
why: Political argument and personal perspective on Chinese history and government; no technical lesson.

title: Account of a college protest incident
why: Political and factual dispute about a campus incident; argumentative rather than instructive.

title: Meta-argument about disagreement and confidence
why: Rambling meta-discussion about online disagreement with no concrete explanation a reader would learn from.

title: Constitutional argument about federal regulation
why: Political and legal argument about constitutional interpretation; opinion-driven rather than explanatory.

title: Why US metro parking lots hurt ridership
why: Sprawling park-and-ride stations serve few riders, and height limits cap density, so driving often beats transit in US cities.

title: Rant about bloated web apps
why: Opinion and frustration about web app performance and nostalgia for old software; no concrete lesson.

title: Advice on choosing a college
why: General advice and personal opinion about college choice; reasonable but not a specific technical or informational lesson.

title: Personal account of a failed Google interview
why: Personal interview anecdote and frustration; describes an experience without a broadly transferable lesson.

title: Speculation about war and sanctions

title: Why copyright is hard to codify and apply

title: Fear about police drones and helicopters

title: Personal career dilemma in Brazil
why: Personal career and life dilemma with no general lesson a reader would learn.

title: ITS and the hacker aesthetic of total machine control
why: Early MIT hackers resisted timesharing because controlling the whole machine mattered; ITS shows that era's culture and shared-machine design.

title: Why Linux's GPLv2-only license and ABI exception matter
why: Linux is GPLv2-only to block upgrade clauses, and its syscall ABI exception means userspace programs need not be GPL-licensed.

title: Signed lease clauses are not always enforceable
why: Signing a lease does not make every clause enforceable, and tenants keep statutory rights even when the lease omits them.

title: Why flexible office landlords charge more
why: Leveraged landlords want long leases; flexible operators take short-term risk, so they charge a premium and compete on services instead of price.

title: Personal experience switching between Mac and Windows
why: Personal platform preference and back-and-forth experience; anecdotal with no transferable lesson.

title: Why restarts make Lisp's condition system stronger

why: Argumentative fact-check disputing an article's claims; it lists courses but teaches no concept.

title: Most UK CCTV cameras are privately owned
why: Estimates put UK cameras near 1.85M, about 92% privately owned and mostly deterring theft at commercial premises, not state watching.

why: Run systemd-analyze security on a unit to list hardening flags and exposure scores, then apply options like PrivateTmp and NoNewPrivileges.

title: Opinion on research universities and teaching
why: Personal opinion about research versus teaching in universities; argumentative rather than explanatory.

why: Experienced lifeguard notes non-approved floats hide children and poor pool sightlines stop guards and parents from seeing swimmers.

why: NSF, NIH and other agencies fund different kinds of labor, and a diversity of funding structures is needed because research output is hard to measure.

title: Monads let pure functions model side effects
